Two points:

> What i don’t love is your attitude toward your proposal, or your performance over this year, and i dont think you have really lived up to your promise to launching kabocha in any sort of dedicated way, I actually think you have abandoned your duty to Kabocha, and youve been quite disruptive, even if you write the occasional good post. 

You are welcome to that opinion. 

My role as a steward has been to make Kabocha a thing, to instigate its inception, establish its positioning, introduce its core technical insights, to organise people and proposals and to communicate that within the edgeware community and wider substrate ecosystem.

Kabocha is not a thing yet. 

We are waiting for it to move to democracy. Nothing else happens until that moment, there is plenty I'm working on, but that doesn't really concern you, such is the beautiful nature of these open source systems with permissionless contribution and governance. 

> Honestly, I rarely getangry, however i will be better at not taking the hominem attcks on my integrity so personally. What you did though is make my life very hard and refuse essentially to talk to me or work with me. This is the kind of games i got to deal with. This has been a struggle for me over the past 2 months. Complete loss of cooperation. 

It's very simple ramsey. I wasn't getting any useful work done on kabocha or edgeware and I found my time and energy being drained by our interactions. 

I sent you a very considered message privately that outlined my concerns and issues and how I was finding it hard to work with you. 

I'm happy to repost it publicly if you are, but in the end, what I aimed to be something that you might reflect on or find encouragement in, was met with more vitriol. 

I didn't want to respond to that - more wasted time and energy, and then you demanded I call you.

I have had a tough year personally, I have a young family, and plenty of other commitments to talented people who do not cause me this level

- Introducing Parachain incubator model to Kusama and Polkadot

- Open ended payment without clear deliverables, can instead become a fixed length contract with deliverables. The contract can always be repeated. But fixed length allows for improvements and accountability. 

- Vague (or weak) proof of agreement, which is currently a sentence or paragraph from a previous proposal, has become our shabby way to form "mandates". This can turn into community approved agreement, structured and titled as a contract.

Reading a lot of the above, it seems a lot of what you do falls into the category of "partnerships" and "network development" (similar to business development). - Clearer responsibilities and duties required.

It seems we are generally as a community lacking on the upfront agreement side of things, and compensating with a lot of justifications (in the futile hope of avoiding dispute) when it comes to the invoicing. If the upfront agreement was stronger then the invoice can be clear and simple. 

I recommend moving forward pre-agreement and post-paid proposals go through referendum and become community approved before any invoices are made. The referendum would not be a funding proposal, it is instead a community vote on the agreement, thus creating a consensus on the agreement. 

There are also some things in there which seem extraneous. It comes across like you are asking to be paid for a lot of planning, ideas and thinking? Most of the "Parachain Incentives" area are basically aims and thoughts. Im not sure these need to be in an invoice? Payment should really be made for quantifiable delivery else we really just open the door to justifying payment for almost anything that is hard to define. 

Moving forward i recommend we use your future contract as one of the first to go through a referendum on the agreement contract, which can help to set a greater standard for agreements.

If we don't understand it it doesn't make us wrong and you right. Thats not the best way to frame this. Everything can be distilled to a simple, understandable idea. 

This agreement structure currently misses the mark on clarity, delivery, accountability, duty and responsibility. If i were a newcomer and read this i would think that Edgeware would fund anything, and would accept a very low standard to pay $10k per month. 

Best thing to do is get a grant form Web 3 Foundation and then Edgeware could partially fund it. That way there at least a verifiable bar. 

> In an ad agency a 'planner' is someone who leads strategy - that involves breaking down a client brief and then figuring out how to frame a particular problem for the creative team to then respond with a concrete response. They are generally the best paid people in the place, since often figuring out the right problem to address, is more important than just making something that might seem useful, but ultimately doesn't really stack up when it comes to moving the needle on things.

This isn't an ad agency (or Madmen) and there are no clients with big contracts produce an ad campaign at the end of it. (In those situations there are also tangible results and measurable impact.) 

I just want to point out that you refer to the old world when you see fit, but if anyone else refers to the old world then they are quickly corrected by you. Its important as you are leader who is paid the most to be self-aware and make sure you adopt the same standards with yourself and others. 


> R&D is what I have done pretty much my whole career - i get your point, but R&D can be applied to anything and everything.

This is my point. Then anyone working on anything they are doing can frame their interests and be paid as RnD. That is one of the reasons I dont support structuring things in this way. And as you are an influential figure in this community you should be leading by example. If the above is a report on what you have delivered, the standard and quality of this structure is substandard even for the present standard.

There is no clear duty and responsibility, it seems like an avoidance of it, yet you are being paid the most. How is that setting an example to others? 


_There are also some things in there which seem extraneous. It comes across like you are asking to be paid for a lot of planning, ideas and thinking?_
> Yes. Exactly.
> That's what I do, and yes, that is what I am charging for

Wouldnt we all love to be paid for just that, but everyone has to deal, do and deliver on things, why do you think you are an exception?

I am little surprised no one else has commented on this. I think it goes over most people's head. It is also not surprising you don't yet see a need for on-chain agreements. 

The section "Parachain Incentives" looks like an unfinished draft of a business plan. And that is the only thing that you shared for V1 of your draft. This shows that you are doing what everyone else does, scrape through some funding doing the minimum. There is nothing wrong with this. However, this shows that you are not holding yourself to a high standard that you set for yourself, which is a shame given the way you critique other peoples proposals. I would expect something of far higher quality. Something we can look at and emulate. 


> [On-chain agreements ] The issue is, this doesn't solve the problem - it just creates two separate steps, that are not binding to each other - unless im not understanding?

The problem is that there is no clear consensus on what is an agreement and contract in the context of decentralised approval. An agreement with on-chain consensus is thus unarguably community approved. Invoice then references an on-chain agreement. I had problems with my last invoice where people disputed that my agreement was in fact an agreement. I am now disputing the above invoice and the fact it was an agreement in the first place. I think the reference to an agreement you shared is not clear, vague with no proper deliverables. I dont think this should be used again to request payment. 


> The approach of preferendums (per Dgen) is the only way I think we can make this better...

I have also spoken to Dgen and Matthieu about preferendums which is useful for making democratic decisions on direction, but that solves a different problem to the one on consensus on agreemeents.

I think in summary, if we boil it down, it seems like you don't want to feel like you have to wake up in the morning and have a duty and responsibility to deliver on promises. You prefer to just be paid to work however and whenever. And i understand the appeal of that. But asking to be paid the highest with this attitude is not palatable.

body:
Hi Rich,

I find this proposal hard to follow, too open ended with no clear deliverables and timelines on what you are doing.

It would help if you broke it up into:

1. What is going to be potentially open ended (R&D)
2. What is ongoing maintenance (eg community management) 
3. What projects you are working on that are actually going to be delivered & by when. 


I see you are working with a few projects so for transparency it would help to list each with the following questions answered:

1. What is the project? (short description / link)
2. What are the milestones? (short description)
3. What are the ETA's on completion for each milestone &  which individual/s is working on it? (name/s, date - only)
4. What is your involvement with the team and what are you doing to help them? (you might be listed as responsible on a milestone?)


The projects / milestones section for your proposal should probably just be a rolling excel template or whatever that just gets marked off as milestones get completed. This would mean you dont have to repeat yourself each month when you go for funding and just update the sheet for example marking the milestones in green when they get completed.

Hey moony. No worries, i'll break it down below and then update the post accordingly.

To be clear, this is a post-paid request, so this is for work that has been completed to date and/or ongoing work that will lead to other things happening on hard to predict timelines that will also (aim to) be funded by Kusama and Polkadot. 

I expect Kabocha to remain relatively illiquid for the forseeable, but there are ways to unlock the funding power there which are not immediately obvious.

Having said that, here we go:

- **Open ended (R&D)**


- [ ] Network publics philosophy and framework

- Council review and operations
